Discussion

Instruction

For the dataset you've been using, choose and run the most appropriate sentiment analysis technique or model. Then explain why you think the model you chose is the best for your data and interpret what you learn from the results.

For this sentiment analysis, I decided to use VADER. This type of sentiment analysis is commonly used and quite robust. Apart from other things highlighted in this analysis, I wanted to see if the sentiment score for the posts increases as the number of retweets or favorite increases. Also see what side of sentimentality is it leaning towards (positive, negative, or neutral). Therefore, i combined metadata comparison with my VADER sentiment analysis to get a more insightful information. The plots show how the metadata and vader_compound (overall sentiment score) relate to each other.

What I learned from this analysis: Going by overall score (vader_compund), I see that posts usually lean towards negative and postive sentiments, and then some are neutral. The neutral posts do not seem to touch on a specific or personal statement. However, posts surrounding depression, anxiety, exhaustion, or sleep typically leaned towards a more negative sentiment. While, post revolving around overcoming challenges, forgiveness, growth and believe had more positive sentiment. For example a post talking about making gifts has a high positve sentiment score of 0.9337. Just to put in perspective.

0.00 is typically neutral. Any post with a - is negative, especially when close to or exactly -1. By that same reasoning, posts leaning upwards of 0.00 are seen as slightly to complety positve (if close to or is exactly 1).

As for the visualization, both plots showed overlapping data points. It just means that a lot of the retweets and favorites (in their respective plots, have the same overall sentiment scoring or extremely close scores.

The retweet vs sentiment plot shows a lean towards a positive relationship. This may mean that the posts that got higher retweets, also had higher or more positve sentiment scores. I would not say it is generally a strong relationship, but it is slightly positive relationship. The plots also show outliers and overlapping data points. Some of the outliers show that some of the highly retweeted posts had low sentiment scores (negative or slightly negative) and it may indicate that other factors may influence retweets, asides from sentiments. Could be factors such as clarity or how coherent the post it, enough so to get a sense of its sentiment.

For favorites vs sentiment, the plot shows a lot of overlapping data. There are a lot of post favorited that leaned anywhere from positve to neutral to negative. I would say however, the highest favorited posts leaned more towards positive sentiments. To me, this plot is less clear. It is possible that other users favorited the posts based on their own personal sentiment. However, the higher the favorites or likes on a post, the more it is more likely to lean away from a total negative sentiment score.

That is to say, people will generally retweet or like more positive posts on social media. However, it depends not only on the sentiment of the posts, but on how the 2nd party (other twitter users) are feeling or if they simply just relate to the posts. Our plots show us that higher retweets tend to have a positive or neutral sentiment, and for favorites it depends; but the higher the number of "likes," the more the sentiment scores leans away from total negative. The printed out sentiment vs metadata scores (not the plots), further confirms my insights.
